heading.en: Laughing at the studio, and at himself

hook.en: Asokamitran's memoir is full of gentle jokes. Underneath the humour, though, he says serious things about talent, ambition and the film world.

objectives.en: Identify the humour and irony in the text
Discuss the themes of the memoir
Comment on the author's tone and self-mockery

narration.en: Asokamitran's memoir is full of gentle jokes. Underneath the humour, though, he says serious things about talent, ambition and the film world.

body.en: The author's humour is gentle and often ironic. He calls the make-up department a model of national integration, describes a middle-aged man as an office boy, and treats his own job of cutting newspaper clippings as something everyone thought was no work at all. The English poet's speech, which no one understood, becomes a comic moment.

points.en: Irony: an office boy who is middle-aged
Mock praise: national integration in the make-up room
Self-mockery: his own job seen as doing nothing
Comic scene: the poet nobody understood

say.en: At the centre is the film world, seen from behind the scenes.
The memoir is told with gentle, witty humour.
Irony runs through it, from the office boy to the poet nobody understood.
Many dreamt of fame but ended up in small roles.
The office boy's envy falls on Subbu.
People from many regions worked together.
The visits show the anti-communist mood of the time.

body.en: Beneath the humour lie real themes: the gap between ambition and achievement, envy and frustration in the workplace, the many people behind a film, and the politics of the time, especially the fear of communism. The title itself joins the creative (poets) and the commercial (pancake make-up) sides of the film world.

problem.en: Give two examples of the author's gentle humour in Poets and Pancakes.

steps.en: Example 1: calling the mixed-region make-up team national integration.
Example 2: a middle-aged man known as the office boy.
Add a note on tone: amused, never cruel.

answer.en: He jokes that the make-up room, staffed by people from many regions, was a model of national integration, and he notes that the office boy was a middle-aged man. His humour is amused and gentle, never cruel.
